613: You are in the matrix (pH ≈ 7.8), between the cristae: Krebs cycle, β-oxidation, pyruvate dehydrogenase, mitochondrial DNA, mitoribosomes. The cristae carry the respiratory chain: complexes I (blue), II (purple), III (green), IV (pink); ATP synthases (orange) line up as dimers along their rims. Yellow dots: electrons; white dots: protons; green dots: ATP. Tap a complex for its card.
615: A lamellar fold of the inner membrane (lumen ≈ 20 nm), connected to the peripheral inner membrane by narrow crista junctions held by the MICOS complex. A membrane very rich in protein (≈ 75 % of its mass) and in cardiolipin. Pumped protons build up in the crista lumen: proton-motive force ≈ 180–200 mV. Mobile carriers are not shown: ubiquinone in the membrane, cytochrome c (12 kDa) on the lumen side.
617: 45 subunits, ≈ 1 MDa, L-shaped. Matrix arm: NADH → FMN → chain of iron-sulfur clusters → ubiquinone. Membrane arm: pumps 4 H⁺ per electron pair. Seven subunits (ND1–ND6, ND4L) are encoded by mitochondrial DNA. Associated with III₂ and IV in a “respirasome”. Inhibited by rotenone; its deficiencies cause Leigh syndrome or Leber hereditary optic neuropathy.
619: Four subunits (SDHA to SDHD), all nuclear-encoded. The only enzyme shared by the Krebs cycle and the respiratory chain: succinate → fumarate, electrons to FAD, three iron-sulfur clusters then ubiquinone. Pumps no protons. SDHx variants: hereditary paragangliomas and phaeochromocytomas.
621: An obligate dimer, 11 subunits per monomer (cytochrome b is encoded by mitochondrial DNA). Through the Q cycle it oxidises ubiquinol, reduces cytochrome c and transfers 4 H⁺ per electron pair to the crista lumen. Inhibited by antimycin A.
623: 13 to 14 subunits (COX1 to COX3 encoded by mitochondrial DNA). It receives electrons from cytochrome c (CuA → haem a → haem a₃–CuB centre) and reduces O₂ to 2 H₂O: this is where the oxygen we breathe is consumed. Pumps 2 H⁺ per electron pair. Inhibited by cyanide, carbon monoxide and azide.
625: A rotary motor: protons cross Fo and turn the c-ring (8 subunits in humans) and the γ shaft; the F₁ head (α₃β₃, matrix side) makes 3 ATP per turn, i.e. ≈ 2.7 H⁺ per ATP. The dimers, angled at about 86°, form rows that bend the rim of the cristae. ATP6 and ATP8 are encoded by mitochondrial DNA. Inhibited by oligomycin.
627: A double-stranded circle of 16,569 bp compacted by TFAM (≈ 100 nm). 37 genes: 13 respiratory chain proteins, 22 tRNAs, 2 rRNAs; its own genetic code (UGA = Trp). Replicated by polymerase γ (POLG) and the helicase Twinkle. Maternal inheritance, heteroplasmy.
628: A 55S ribosome (28S and 39S subunits), richer in protein than in RNA. Docked on the inner membrane, it translates the 13 proteins encoded by mitochondrial DNA and inserts them directly into the membrane (OXA1L).
630: A giant complex (≈ 9 MDa, ≈ 45 nm): E1, E2 core, E3. Pyruvate + CoA + NAD⁺ → acetyl-CoA + CO₂ + NADH: the gateway to the Krebs cycle. Cofactors: thiamine pyrophosphate, lipoate, FAD.
632: An oxidising, Ca²⁺-rich compartment (white dots), about 50 nm wide. Nascent chains enter through the translocon, receive their N-glycans, form their disulfide bonds and fold with the help of chaperones, before leaving for the Golgi in COPII vesicles. Misfolded proteins are sent back to the cytosol and degraded (ERAD).
634: The ribosome, on the cytosolic side, is docked on the Sec61 channel after targeting by SRP. The chain enters unfolded; signal peptidase removes the signal peptide; oligosaccharyltransferase (purple) transfers Glc₃Man₉GlcNAc₂ en bloc onto asparagines of N-X-S/T motifs. BiP (orange), an Hsp70, pulls and folds the chain using ATP.
635: A membrane lectin chaperone (calreticulin is its soluble counterpart). It retains glycoproteins bearing a single terminal glucose; UGGT reglucosylates those still misfolded: this is the quality-control cycle. ERp57 catalyses disulfide bonds there.
636: A transmembrane protein whose luminal coiled-coil domains face each other and keep the two membranes of a cisterna apart (≈ 50 nm).
638: The SERCA pump, a P-type ATPase, brings in 2 Ca²⁺ per ATP: ≈ 0.5 mM in the lumen versus ≈ 100 nM in the cytosol. IP₃ and ryanodine receptors release this calcium on demand.
640: An oxidoreductase with CXXC motifs: it forms, breaks and rearranges disulfide bonds until the pairing is right; it is re-oxidised by Ero1.
642: A protein ready for export, with its N-glycan (green mannoses, blue N-acetylglucosamines). In the erythroblast this is for example the TfR1 receptor. It will be concentrated at exit sites by the COPII coat (Sec23/24, Sec13/31).
644: A type II membrane protein: short cytosolic tail, stem, catalytic domain in the lumen. It transfers a sugar from a nucleotide sugar (UDP-GlcNAc, UDP-Gal, CMP-sialic acid…) imported by an antiporter. Each cisterna has its own set of enzymes, hence sequential maturation.
